title: Weather Hazards
seo_title: Grade 3 Weather Hazards Worksheets: Floods, Hurricanes, Tornadoes and Design Solutions
standard_text: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on weather hazards (NGSS 3-ESS3-1): floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, lightning, blizzards and droughts, solutions that reduce damage, and judging solutions with data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: We cannot stop storms, but we can reduce the damage.
key_sub: Levees, storm shelters, lightning rods and other designs protect people. Use evidence to judge which solution works best.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather hazards are dangerous weather events: floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, lightning, blizzards and droughts. People cannot stop them, but they can design solutions that reduce the damage.

  • Floods: levees, houses on posts, storm drains.
  • Hurricanes: storm shutters, strapped roofs, evacuation routes.
  • Tornadoes: storm shelters, warning sirens.
  • Lightning: lightning rods; go indoors.
  • Blizzards: snowplows, snow fences. Droughts: rain barrels, saving water.

To make a claim about a solution's merit, compare evidence: Does it reduce the damage? How much does it cost?

Example

Which solution helps with lightning?

Lightning strikes tall buildings.

Answer: a lightning rod

Example

Flooded homes went from 40 to 10 after a levee was built. Did the levee help?

Fewer homes flooded.

Answer: Yes.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking people can stop storms.
  • Choosing a solution made for a different hazard.
  • Picking the cheapest solution without checking if it protects well.

faq.a: Dangerous weather such as floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, lightning, blizzards and droughts.

faq.q: How do people reduce damage from weather hazards?
faq.a: They build levees, storm shelters and lightning rods, use storm shutters, clear snow and save water.

faq.q: How do you judge a design solution?
faq.a: Look at evidence, like how much damage happened before and after, and compare the cost and protection.
